title: Can Riverlane's Deltaflow Unlock Useful Quantum Computing?
excerpt: Can Riverlane’s Deltaflow unlock useful quantum computing?
content:
By 2026, Riverlane aims to achieve a critical milestone for practical quantum computing: a million real-time quantum operations, known as MegaQuOps, the company says. This threshold, the company reports, is where quantum computers can begin running their first error-corrected applications. Deltaflow 2, Riverlane’s quantum error correction stack, will perform real-time error correction on up to 250 physical qubits using its proprietary Local Clustering Decoder. The system processes petabytes of data through readout processing, a powerful decoder, and an orchestration layer to transform unstable qubits into reliable logical qubits.

Deltaflow Enables MegaQuOp Computing by 2026

This decoder, broken into smaller sections, processes data in parallel to maintain speed while tackling the escalating number of qubit errors inherent in quantum systems. Deltaflow’s orchestration layer coordinates this complex activity in real time, integrating readout processing from any quantum computer control system with the powerful decoder.

The company states that crossing into the MegaQuOp regime presents a central moment in quantum computing, where the power of quantum computers goes beyond the reach of any classical supercomputer. The development of Deltaflow is not occurring in isolation; Riverlane actively partners with leading quantum computer manufacturers to tailor the error correction stack to specific hardware.

This collaborative process begins with a deep understanding of each partner’s qubits, hardware and error characteristics, followed by the design of optimal error correction codes and decoders. Riverlane partner to test and implement QEC solutions offline in software, and then test and implement real-time QEC solutions in hardware, with support from a contract with the UK’s National Quantum Computing Centre.

Riverlane also collaborates with Oak Ridge National Laboratory to improve the integration of High Performance Computing (HPC) with quantum systems, further demonstrating a commitment to improving the integration of these technologies, according to the company. The company’s approach centers on building a comprehensive quantum error correction stack, capable of handling the immense data processing demands of scaling quantum computers to useful levels of performance.
